text:
Evidence supports testing the objective before adding residual gates, but does not establish the bottleneck in Electronics. The [original NextItNet paper](https://fajieyuan.github.io/papers/nextitnet6.pdf) explicitly supports sampled-softmax training. [Wu et al., TOIS 2024](https://wujcan.github.io/papers/tois-ssm.pdf) identify sampled softmax’s implicit hard-negative weighting and ranking benefits, while warning that cosine normalization can restrict representation-magnitude learning. [gBCE research, IJCAI 2024](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0939) shows that sampled BCE can cause overconfidence and unstable training; its empirical evidence concerns SASRec/BERT4Rec, so transfer to NextItNet remains a hypothesis.

Uniform sampling is a defensible first comparison. A [2024 sequential-recommendation study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) finds substantial accuracy/popularity trade-offs across uniform, popularity, in-batch and adaptive samplers. [Hard-negative theory](https://doi.org/10.1145/3543507.3583223) supports controllable hardness rather than universally choosing the hardest candidates. [UFNRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04116) documents false-negative risks, although its teacher-based remedy should not be copied under this task’s single-model constraint. The search found no direct NextItNet evidence establishing a moderate-hard curriculum as superior.

Practical hypothesis: keep the ungated NextItNet backbone fixed; compare multi-negative BCE against sampled-softmax cross-entropy using identical uniform candidate sets and negative counts, optionally adding gBCE. Exclude padding, the target and known training-history positives; deduplicate candidates without consulting held-out labels. These safeguards remove known collisions, not all latent false negatives. Only after establishing the uniform baseline, test a uniform warm-up followed by a small fraction of moderately high-scoring candidates from the same model. This curriculum is an experimental proposal, not a demonstrated result; select using the pinned macro validation HR@10.
